author: Megan Viecelli
title: Wellness Wednesday: Revenge bedtime procrastination - NewsBreak
text:
By Megan Viecelli ,
7 hours ago
LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) – Do you ever find yourself staying up later than you planned? Scrolling on your phone or watching “just one” more episode?
After a long day of work, responsibilities and constant demands, many of us look forward to the late-night hours because it’s the only real personal time we get.
But that can lead to something experts call “revenge bedtime procrastination” — the habit of delaying sleep to reclaim your time.
Psychologists say it often happens when people feel like their daytime schedule is packed with obligations, leaving little room for relaxation or control.
So, even when we’re tired, we end up staying up late because it feels like the only time that truly belongs to us.
But the problem is that sacrificing sleep can catch up to us quickly, leading to fatigue, difficulty concentrating, irritability and increased stress the next day.
Experts say one way to break the cycle is to create small moments of personal time earlier in the evening, instead of waiting until bedtime. This could be taking a short walk, reading, calling a friend or spending a few minutes doing something relaxing without screens.
Another helpful step is setting a consistent wind-down routine. Try dimming the lights, putting away your phone and giving your brain time to transition toward sleep.
Because while staying up late might make you feel like you’re taking back control of your time, you’re more likely to feel more energized and overall balanced the next day if you protect your sleep.
